_comment: End-to-end agent questions for SuSchedule-r. Assertions link facts to course codes, restrict unexpected course-code mentions, and optionally require semantic trace actions. Ground truth is taken from the SU catalog and offerings data. Run through scheduler.session.PlannerSession in react mode with transcript_cagan.json loaded.

questions.q: I am comparing workload for next term. Please look up CS 412 from the catalog and tell me only how many SU credits it carries.
Before I plan around CS 301, check the official prerequisite rule and tell me which courses I must have completed.
Can you check CS 307 specifically and explain its prerequisite in one concise sentence?
What does CS 445 cover? I want a smooth explanation of the course content, not a raw catalog dump.
Does CS 411 require any math prerequisite? Please check the catalog rule and name the math course if there is one.
I saw CS 412 in the catalog. Is it actually a machine learning course, and what kind of ML topics does it introduce?
Give me a short student-friendly explanation of what CS 307 is about and what systems topics it covers.
Using my loaded transcript context, recommend one theoretical computer science elective that could make sense for me. Explain why it fits theory, but do not create a full semester plan.
I want to deepen my computer networks knowledge. Recommend one relevant course from the catalog, explain what it covers, and keep it as advice rather than a committed plan.
For scheduling purposes, check whether CS 412 has a required recitation or lab component.
If I try to take CS 412 and CS 302 together in the target term, can the system find a conflict-free timetable including their recitations?
I enjoy optimization and operations research. Suggest one catalog course I could explore, and avoid unrelated courses that only mention optimization casually.

I clicked the Check Schedule button. Please review my current builder schedule, including recitations/labs, time conflicts, total SU credits, and whether the choices look reasonable for my loaded CS degree context.
